questions.stem: Which word best describes how likely this is? You will breathe today.
worked: Breathing today must happen.
Something that must happen is certain.

questions.stem: Which word best describes how likely this is? You will roll a 7 on a standard die.
worked: The faces of a standard die are 1 to 6, so a 7 cannot happen.
Something that cannot happen is impossible.

questions.stem: Which word best describes how likely this is? It will rain somewhere in Britain this week.
worked: Rain somewhere in Britain in a week happens far more often than not.
It is not guaranteed, so it is likely, not certain.

questions.stem: Which word best describes how likely this is? You will flip heads on a fair coin.
worked: A fair coin has 2 equally likely outcomes, and heads is 1 of them.
1 out of 2 is an even chance.

questions.stem: Which word best describes how likely this is? A randomly chosen month starts with J.
worked: January, June and July start with J: 3 of the 12 months.
3 out of 12 is less than half, so it is unlikely.

questions.stem: Which word best describes how likely this is? You pick a red card from a standard pack.
worked: Half the cards in a standard pack are red: 26 of 52.
Half is an even chance.

questions.stem: Which word best describes how likely this is? You roll an even number on a die.
worked: 2, 4 and 6 are even: 3 of the 6 faces.
3 out of 6 is a half, an even chance.

questions.stem: Which word best describes how likely this is? You win the lottery with one ticket.
worked: One ticket has about a 1 in 45 million chance of winning.
It could happen, so it is not impossible, but it is very unlikely.

questions.stem: Which word best describes how likely this is? A baby born today is a boy.
worked: Boys and girls are born in very nearly equal numbers.
So it is about an even chance.

questions.stem: Which word best describes how likely this is? The sun will rise tomorrow.
worked: The sun rises every day.
So it is certain.

questions.stem: Which of these statements is true?

options.label: If P(rain) = 0.4, it will rain on exactly 4 out of every 10 days
P(event) is always between 0 and 1 inclusive

worked: Probability ranges from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).
It can never be negative or greater than 1.

slip.line: P(rain) = 0.4 means that over a very large number of days, about 40% will have rain. But in any specific set of 10 days, it could rain on 0, 1, 2, ... or even all 10 days.
Probability can never exceed 1. The maximum probability is 1 (certain) and the minimum is 0 (impossible).

options.label: A probability of 0.9 means the event will definitely happen

worked: The probability of an event not happening is 1 minus the probability of it happening.

worked: This is the gambler's fallacy.
